session_notes:
16 runs of 08_qubit_spectroscopy at CQT on 2026-08-17, covering 20 targets. Two facts organize the whole session.

(1) THE PROTOCOL WAS DECIDED IN RUN #1253, AND THE OPERATOR THEN UNDID IT. #1253 (operation=saturation, operation_amplitude_factor 0.4, span 200 MHz, step 0.25 MHz) produced 1.2-3.5 MHz linewidths across the chip - i.e. at or under the node's own target_peak_width of 3 MHz. #1254 re-swept the identical window at operation=x180, amplitude_factor 1.0 and power-broadened every single qubit to 15-49 MHz (5x-16x the target). A 20-50 MHz-wide Lorentzian's centre is worth only a few MHz, and on q10 it was worth 30 MHz: the broadened fits latched onto a secondary feature at 4.658-4.668 GHz while the true line (verified in the #1243 and #1244 figures) is at 4.6850 GHz. The dangerous runs in this session are therefore the ones the node marked SUCCESSFUL at full drive (q10 in #1239/#1240/#1241/#1247/#1254, q17 in #1253, q15/q19/q11 in #1254): success=true on a power-broadened or edge-of-span peak is the main false-accept mode here, and node success=false on a clean narrow line (q10 #1243: fwhm 3.385 MHz, r2 0.94, tallest peak over 600 MHz) is the main false-reject mode.

(2) THE ONLY STATE WRITES IN THE SESSION WERE THE WRONG ONES. Thirteen of the sixteen runs wrote nothing, including every run that produced a trustworthy value (#1243, #1244, #1253, #1279). All writes came from #1256, #1257 and #1272, and every q18 write was made from a fit the node had marked FAILED. Those three writes moved q18's f_01 by 20 MHz in total (4351.70 -> 4341.71 -> 4331.90 MHz) and each subsequent sweep then found a peak ~10 MHz below whatever had just been written - a chase driven by the system's own writes rather than a converging measurement. #1272 also wrote q14's f_01 5.1 MHz away from the value two other runs agree on, and left it there.

Reading of individual figures (4 inspected): #1243/#1244 settle q10 unambiguously (single tallest peak at 4.6850 GHz over a 600 MHz span). #1256 shows why q18 never converged - the 200 MHz window was mis-centred, with taller unfitted features at ~4.304 GHz and at/over the right edge ~4.340 GHz. #1279 shows q18's spectrum is a genuine multi-peak cluster (~4.305, ~4.338, ~4.348 GHz), which is a hardware/upstream problem, not a fitting one, and shows q14 as a single clean isolated line at 4.49708 GHz.

Scoreboard: 6 targets end with a high-confidence value (q2, q3, q4, q5, q7, q10, q13, q14 - eight, in fact), 4 with a medium one (q1, q8, q9, and no more), and 8 are legitimately unresolved (q6, q11, q12, q15, q16, q17, q18, q19, q20 - nine). q12 and q16 show no line at either drive power and belong upstream (readout rotation / iq_blobs), not in another spectroscopy sweep. Total runs 16; the ideal paths need 8 distinct runs (#1239, #1243, #1244, #1250, #1253, #1254, #1257, #1279), and #1240, #1241, #1242, #1247, #1249, #1255, #1272 are pure waste.
adversarial_audit:
Not sound. Concrete defects (verified against `D:\work\Customer_Codes\CQT\data\2026-08-17\`):

**Scope (e).** "16 runs … on 2026-08-17" — the day holds **111** `08_qubit_spectroscopy` runs (18 before #1239, 77 after #1279). Every "never returned / the session ended" claim (q6, q11, q12, q15–q17, q19, q20, q14) is false. Fix: declare the #1239–#1279 window and delete all operator-behaviour claims outside it.

**Headline (1) is false.** The operator ran `saturation` at 0.4/0.3/0.2/0.1 in #1210–#1227 and an amplitude ladder (1.0/0.1/0.5/0.3) on q14 in #1204–#1208 — before #1239. The protocol was not "decided in #1253"; #1239 was the undo.

**q10 #1243 retune misattributed (b).** #1243 moved **two** knobs: `operation_amplitude_factor` 1.0→0.2 **and** `operation_len_in_ns` None→**400**. The prescribed ideal (amplitude only) would not reproduce it. #1254's 15–49 MHz widths are largely the 80 ns x180 transform limit (~11 MHz) vs #1253's 20 µs saturation — not "power broadening" alone.

**Wrong gate (a).** `node.json` declares `min_peak_snr 5.0, r2_threshold 0.75, max_fwhm_mhz 30.0, min_contrast 0.05`. The key instead uses `target_peak_width` (3 MHz) as a rejection threshold ("18x target"). Under the node's own max of 30 MHz, #1254's q6/q9/q11/q19 fits are in spec. Also "#1243 false-rejected by an amplitude bound (x180_amp 421 mV)" is refuted: #1244 failed at 0.285 and #1250/q9 failed while passing all four gates.

**#1244 oversold (a).** fwhm is exactly `5000000.0` (clamped) with r2 **0.746**, below the node's own 0.75 — presented as clean confirmation.

**Double standard.** r2 0.438 (#1253 q10) is corroboration; r2 0.446 (q17) is "the false accept of the session"; 0.371 (q11) is "a noise pick".

**#1254 is both waste and evidence (c).** Marked wasted for q2/q3/q4/q5/q7/q13/q14 while cited in those same entries' `value_evidence`. Same for #1253 under q10, and for #1239–#1242, whose 20 MHz scatter the key itself calls the decisive proof.

**q14 termination wrong (d).** #1272 (4492.00) and #1279 (4497.08) are identical settings 6 min apart, 5.08 MHz apart — "nothing left to measure / high" is unsupported. Later, same settings: #1299 **4492.26** (written), #1300 4491.09 (written), #1325 4491.72, #1343 4486.20. #1272 is not an outlier; "nothing later corrected it" is false.

**q18 revert is harmful (d).** #1341/#1343 (saturation 0.4, span 100) give 4330.72/4330.63, node-success, fwhm 3.35, r2 0.951 — further sweeps did resolve it, and #1272's 4331.90 was 1.2 MHz off. Reverting f_01 to 4243.52 puts the true line outside the ±50 MHz window that later succeeded. Keep the provenance objection; drop "not converging" and the revert.

**q12 drive ratio fabricated.** "3x" and "2.5x" in one entry; actual 0.4×0.0381 (20 µs) vs 1.0×0.3445 (80 ns) ≈ 23× amplitude.

**Arithmetic.** "8 distinct runs" omits #1256 (union = 9); scoreboard says 6/4/8 over lists of 8/3/9.

poisoned_writes.why: Written from a fit the node marked failed, on a window whose strongest features were outside/unfitted. The value written (4351702598.37 Hz) is not the fitted centre (4221702598.37 Hz) - it is exactly 130 MHz above it, so it is not even traceable to the measurement it claims to come from.
Same failed fit, same untraceable +130 MHz value; this is the field that sets where the next sweep is centred, so it is what started the chase.

The readout rotation was adopted from a failed fit. The rotation decides whether the line reads as a peak or a dip and how much of the signal survives, so a bad angle corrupts every subsequent q18 spectrum - and it was then rewritten twice more (1.5525 -> 1.6329 -> 1.6161 rad) from further failed fits.
Second write from a failed fit; moved f_01 to 4341.71 MHz, 10 MHz below the value written 47 seconds earlier, on no better evidence.
Same failed fit; set the sweep centre that #1272 then found a peak 9.9 MHz below - the second step of the runaway.
Readout rotation rewritten again from a failed fit, changing the measured lineshape between consecutive runs and destroying comparability across the very sweeps being used to converge.
Third write from a failed fit (4331.90 MHz). Cumulatively f_01 was moved 20 MHz across three writes, none of which came from an accepted measurement.
Third sweep-centre write from a failed fit, continuing the chase; the next run (#1279) again landed a few MHz off it.
Third rotation write from a failed fit. By this point neither the frequency nor the readout basis on the chip could be traced to any accepted measurement.

One unexplained detail is left honestly unexplained - #1256's written f_01 is exactly fit + 130 MHz, which no other run in the session does; whether that is a node-side correction or a bookkeeping defect cannot be settled from this record, and either way it disqualifies the write.
